content: Calcium phosphate refers to a group of minerals that contain calcium ions (Ca²⁺) combined with orthophosphates (PO₄³⁻), metaphosphates, or pyrophosphates (P₂O₇⁴⁻), and sometimes hydrogen or hydroxide ions. It is the primary form of calcium found in bovine milk and blood. Approximately 70% of bone is composed of hydroxyapatite, a calcium phosphate mineral also known as bone mineral. Tooth enamel is made up of nearly 90% hydroxyapatite. Unlike most other compounds, the solubility of calcium phosphate decreases as temperature increases, leading to precipitation when heated. In milk, calcium phosphate exists in higher concentrations than would normally be possible at the standard pH because it is present in a colloidal form within micelles bound to casein protein, along with magnesium, zinc, and citrate. This complex is collectively referred to as colloidal calcium phosphate (CCP). Calcium phosphate is utilized in the production of phosphoric acid and fertilizers, such as in the Odda process. However, excessive use of certain forms of calcium phosphate can result in nutrient-rich surface runoff, which can negatively impact aquatic ecosystems by causing algal blooms and eutrophication. It is also used in baking as the acidic component of leavening agents, identified by the E number E341, and in cheese products. A supersaturated calcium phosphate solution, such as Caphosol, is employed in the prevention and treatment of oral mucositis caused by chemotherapy or radiotherapy. Tricalcium phosphate is used as a nutritional supplement and occurs naturally in cow milk. However, the most common and cost-effective forms of calcium supplementation are calcium carbonate (which should be taken with food) and calcium citrate (which can be taken without food). Limited studies have been conducted on the use of hydroxyapatite as a food supplement, and its use is generally discouraged. Calcium phosphate is incorporated into various dental products for remineralization and is also used as a diluent in some medications, where it can give tablets a gray color in the absence of additional coloring agents. Another application of calcium phosphate is in gene transfection, where calcium phosphate precipitate forms a complex with DNA, facilitating the entry of DNA into cells. It is also being explored in the development of contrast agents. Biphasic calcium phosphate, a biomaterial consisting of a mixture of tricalcium phosphate and hydroxyapatite, is an alternative to bone grafting. It is used around osseous implants, such as dental implants, and gradually resorbs, being replaced by new vital bone through bone regeneration. Tetracalcium phosphate (Ca₄(PO₄)₂O) and amorphous calcium phosphate, a glassy precipitate of variable composition, may also be present in biological systems.
